pl-l4d44c2-d1e112.summary: Continues Augustine: the earthly matter from which mortal flesh is created is not lost to God; whatever dust or ash it dissolves into, whatever breath or air it flees into, whatever other bodies or elements it turns into, whatever animals' or men's food and flesh, it will return in an instant to the soul that first animated it to become, grow, and live.
claims: All bodily matter returns to its own soul.

pl-l4d44c2-d1e118.summary: Continues: that matter will not be restored so that what dissolved and turned into other things must return to the same bodily parts; else, if all the hair and nails cut off returned, an unseemly deformity would occur to those imagining resurrection. As an artist remaking a melted or crushed statue from its matter need not return each particle to its former member, so God, the wondrous artist, will restore our flesh from all its matter, whether hair returns to hair and nails to nails or is turned into flesh and other parts, providing that nothing unseemly occurs; nothing there will be unfitting.
claims: Matter need not return to the same parts.
God restores the body fittingly, like an artist.

pl-l4d44c2.summary: The earthly matter of mortal flesh is not lost to God: however dissolved, scattered, changed into other substances or into others' flesh, it will return in an instant to the soul that first animated it. Yet it need not return to the same parts: as an artist remaking a melted statue need not return each particle to its former member, so God, the wondrous artist, will restore the flesh from all its matter, turning lost hair and nails into flesh where fitting, so nothing unseemly results.
claims: No matter of the body is lost to God.
Matter returns to the soul that animated it.
It need not return to the same parts; God restores the whole fittingly.
